title: Starter Journey Schematic Jot
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal sketch for a lightweight "starter journey" feature — goal: let teams get a minimal working assistant in front of users in <15 minutes with reasonable defaults (model, prompt templates, cost/day guardrails). This is a thinking-log, not a polished PRD.

High-level idea:
- Provide an opinionated onramp that wires: sample dataset or canned prompts -> selected model bundle -> default routing (hosted) -> simple metrics + rollback.
- Emphasize speed to value: minimal fields, pre-baked templates, one-click deploy to a preview assistant.
- Make it obvious how to graduate to dedicated/private later.

Assumptions (for now):
- Target users: small product/PM/engineer who wants to ship assistant MVP quickly; not enterprise yet.
- Typical goal: proof-of-concept chat/faq flow, sometimes simple form-filling or summarization.
- We can pick 2 model profiles (fast-cheap, balanced-quality) as defaults.
- Visibility into per-session cost + token breakdown is critical for trust.

User scenarios (quick):
1) Marketing lead wants a demo assistant to answer product FAQs. Has a markdown FAQ doc. Wants it live for demo.
2) Support engineer wants a summarizer bot for incoming tickets (drop in CSV). Wants to test 50 samples.
3) Internal team wants an interview-bot for candidate prep using canned prompts.

Core flows (sketch):
A) Starter Wizard (3 steps):
  1) Pick a template (FAQ assistant, Summarizer, Q&A from doc, Meeting recap). Short descriptions for each.
  2) Upload content OR paste (docs, CSV, list) + quick mapping (title->context). Offer sample dataset.
  3) Choose a default profile: "Sprint" (low cost, quantized), "Polish" (higher-quality). Toggle for streaming on/off.
  -> click "Preview assistant" which spins up a temporary preview endpoint.
B) Preview UX:
  - Small chat iframe with context toggles (show/hide doc snippets): used to sanity-check recall.
  - Cost estimate banner: tokens/estimated $/hour at expected QPS (very rough).
  - Quick link: "Promote to team" (creates route and basic metrics dashboard).

User stories (examples):
- As a Product Lead, I want to pick an "FAQ" starter and paste our README so I can demo an assistant by EOD.
- As an Engineer, I want a preview endpoint I can curl so I can integrate the assistant into a prototype page.
- As an Operator, I want the wizard to recommend a quantization profile when the dataset is small, so we reduce early costs.

Acceptance / success metrics (initial):
- Time from wizard start -> preview ready < 15 minutes (90th percentile)
- >20 teams complete the wizard in first 2 months of experiment
- Average initial monthly spend per team < $200 (we're intentionally low)
- Preview -> promoted conversion >= 15% (indicates usefulness)

Constraints & guardrails:
- No enterprise features in first iteration (no VPC, no custom KMS). Keep hosted only.
- Strict per-project soft budget with cooldown if surpassed (prevent runaway costs).
- Limit dataset size for preview (e.g., 5MB) to keep inference fast and cheap.

Rough tech considerations / infra notes:
- Reuse existing hosted model routing and default model catalog entry points.
- Temporary preview endpoints should be ephemeral (TTL 24–48h), cost-limited.
- Use prefix/KV caching aggressively for uploaded docs (so multiple requests in preview don't re-tokenize).
- UI: small wizard modal in Console; preview uses same hosted API route with a flag (preview=true) to change routing/cost controls.

Open questions / tradeoffs (stuff to decide):
- Template coverage: start with 4 templates or 6? (Lean towards 4).
- Should we auto-generate prompt templates from uploaded doc? (MVP: provide heuristics + let user pick sample prompts).
- Billing UX: do we charge immediately on preview usage or only once promoted? (prefer soft-credits for preview).
- Model defaults: which two profiles map to our catalog names? Need mapping table.

Experimentation plan (quick):
- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): build wizard UI + 2 templates + preview endpoint + simple cost banner. Manual handoff to 5 internal teams for testing.
- Sprint 2 (2 weeks): add upload mapping UI, per-sample test harness, small metrics tracking for conversion.
- Metrics to log: time-to-preview, preview requests per session, cost per preview, promote clicks, errors.

Prototype ideas for validation (fast):
- Low-fi: Google Doc with short instructions + product engineer manually wires preview. Use to test copy + funnel.
- Mid-fi: Console modal + iframe chat using existing hosted route with preview flag.
- Quick A/B: show cost banner vs no-banner to measure trust/engagement.

Copy + microcopy notes (rough):
- "Preview assistant — runs in a sandbox for 24 hours. We'll estimate your cost, not charge until promotion." (if we choose soft-credits)
- Tooltips: "Polish = higher fidelity; Sprint = lower cost, lower latency"

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Users upload sensitive data to hosted preview. Mitigation: warn explicitly and add checkbox: "I confirm no PII" (temporary). Also limit retention and log redaction.
- Risk: Cost blowouts. Mitigation: default to lowest-cost profile and require explicit opt-in for higher-cost profiles.

Next actions (short):
- Sync with Solutions Eng (Noah) to get 3 internal datasets for testing.
- Quick mapping doc of model-profile -> catalog id (ask Mira).
- Small mock in Figma: 3 screens (template pick, upload, preview) — assign to UX.
- Draft simple Linear tickets: onboarding-wizard-frontend, preview-endpoint-backend, preview-billing-guardrail.

Notes-to-self / reminders:
- Keep language non-technical on the first screen so PMs can use it.
- Consider adding an "Examples" toggle that fills the preview with canned queries. Helps verification.
- Revisit retention policy once we flip from preview -> promoted (one-way copy to project storage).

If we want to make this sticky long-term: surface a small "starter insights" panel after promotion: top queries, token hotspots, where cost concentrated. Low friction immediate value for initial users.

-- end of jot --
